subject: Post-demo: Dataflow & logging masking - next steps
messages:
From: Tara Singh <tara.singh@medlume.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 4 Jul 2025 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Thanks for the demo — logging/dataflow questions

Evelyn,

Thanks for the walkthrough earlier today — the demo was helpful. As we discussed, securing and minimizing sensitive data in the request/response logs is a blocker for our security team before we can move to a POC. A couple of specific follow-ups from our side so we can scope next steps: 

- Can Redwood confirm at a high level which fields are kept in request/response logs by default and what you redact automatically? In particular we need to know how headers (Authorization/Trace-Id/Set-Cookie) are treated.
- Do you offer per-customer configurable masking rules (regex, field names) at ingestion, or is masking applied only post-hoc in the analytics pipeline?
- What's the shortest retention window you support for raw request/response logs? Our default policy is 90 days but we'd like to see options down to 30 days for certain endpoints.
- Would you be able to provide one sanitized sample of a request log that shows header masking + body redaction?

Our security reviewer (cc'd) will need SOC2 and any data flow diagrams you can share.

Next steps we proposed on the call: a short tech deep-dive with engineering + a proposed mutual action plan (deliverables and timeline). Can you send a concise next-step list and any artifacts you have (playbook, sample sanitized logs, recording)?

Thanks — appreciate the quick turnaround.

Tara Singh
Head of Product Security
MedLume Health
Attachment: MedLume_SSCQ.xlsx (questionnaire stub)
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>
To: Tara Singh <tara.singh@medlume.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 4 Jul 2025 17:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Thanks for the demo — logging/dataflow questions

Hi Tara — great to connect earlier. Recap below and suggested next steps. I copied Aditya (sales engineering) and Karthik (inference infra) to own technical details.

Quick answers (summary):
- Default collection: we persist structured request metadata (timestamp, route, model variant, token counts) and a trimmed request/response payload for debugging. Sensitive headers (Authorization, Cookie) are redacted by default at ingress; Trace-Id is kept but can be obfuscated/masked per-customer.
- Masking controls: we provide configurable ingestion rules that operate at ingress (regex and JSON-path masking) and an optional post-ingest sanitization pipeline. Customers can supply a list of headers/fields to redact; we apply rules before logs are written to persistent storage for Private and Dedicated customers.
- Retention windows: hosted customers can configure retention from 30–365 days; Dedicated/Private deployments can set custom retention (can be <30 days in Private on-prem).
- Sample sanitized logs: we'll prepare a redacted sample with trace-id obfuscated (not real values) and send it in the next email.

Proposed immediate next steps (timeline):
1) Security deep-dive (30–45m): engineering + security demo of ingestion & masking — target week of 7/7. (Owner: Karthik)
2) Redaction playbook & sample: we will share our redact/mask patterns and a sanitized request log (Owner: Aditya).
3) Workshop to map MedLume endpoints to masking rules and retention policy; produce a mutual action plan (Owner: Evelyn).

I attached the Redwood log masking playbook and the demo recording. Please let me know availability for the deep-dive and any questions on the short answers above.

Thanks,

Evelyn Hart
Enterprise Sales — Redwood Inference
Attachment: redaction-playbook.pdf, demo-recording.mp4
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 7 Jul 2025 09:12:00 -07:00
Subject: FW: Post-demo: Dataflow & logging masking - next steps (internal)

Team — forwarding Tara's questions and my reply. TL;DR: MedLume needs header-level masking (Authorization, Set-Cookie), Trace-Id obfuscation (customer preference), and a retention policy of 90 days for most routes but they may want 30 days for high-volume telemetry endpoints.

Action items I want us to confirm before the deep-dive:
- Aditya: produce a sanitized sample log (JSON) showing field-level redaction, header stripping, and an obfuscated trace id. Keep the sample small (1–2 requests) and include a short note describing which rules were applied. Target: 7/8 EOD.
- Karthik: confirm how masking is implemented in Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private. We need explicit wording for the security call: "masking applied at ingress before persistent storage" or note exceptions. Also confirm whether trace-id obfuscation can be deterministic for correlation without exposing original values. Target: 7/9 morning.
- Monica: prepare SOC2 & network diagram links for the security folder; ensure we have a point-of-contact in infra for Private deployments if they request on-prem.

Keep it tactical — Tara wants the sanitized sample and an actionable deep-dive calendar invite. I'll handle scheduling once we confirm owners.

Evelyn
From: Tara Singh <tara.singh@medlume.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 7 Jul 2025 12:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo: Dataflow & logging masking - next steps

Evelyn — thanks for the rapid follow-up and the playbook. A couple of clarifications from my security reviewer: 

- Retention: MedLume's baseline is 90 days for debug logs; for user-identifiable telemetry we want 30 days. Can Redwood enforce route-specific retention (90 days for /api/v1/clinical, 30 days for /api/v1/analytics)?
- Trace-Id: we require trace IDs to be present for incident tracing but never in plaintext; an obfuscated deterministic mapping is fine (we need the same obfuscated id across logs to tie traces together).
- Masking audit: security would like a short statement we can include in our vendor assessment that lists what is redacted by default and which controls are configurable.

We're happy to run the deep-dive on 7/9 at 10:00am PT if that works for your engineers. Attendees on our side: me, Chris Park (infrastructure), and our security reviewer (Marcus Lin — cc'd on the attached questionnaire). Please send the sanitized sample before the call so our reviewer can look at it.

Thanks — Tara
